steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Combine the 2 teaspoons of lime juice with the milk, let stand for 5 minutes.

In a large bowl, cream together the butter and 3/4 cup sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg, then stir in the lime zest and milk mixture. Combine the flour, baking powder and baking soda, blend into the creamed mixture. Drop by rounded spoonfuls onto the ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven, until the edges are light brown. Allow cookies to cool on baking sheets for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.
To make the glaze, stir together the remaining lime juice and sugar. Brush onto cooled cookies.

raw_recipe.headline: Spring Lime Tea Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These are light, buttery tea cookies bursting with citrus flavor.

review.reviewBody: Really pretty, soft cookie with a just right taste of refreshing lime. The dough is very soft, so I chilled it until it became firm enough to work with. Made these for hubby's staff for St. Patrick's Day so I tinted the glaze green (made with powdered sugar and lime juice), and sprinkled them with green decorator sugar. They look as good as bakery cookies but taste SO much better!

The perfect tea cookie: lovely texture, not too sweet and so refreshing and light. I wanted more citrus flavor so I used equal amounts of lime and lemon zest, lime and lemon juice and added a packet of unsweetend "True Lemon" water enhancer crystals to the dough. I let the dough chill in the fridge for about an hour before dropping the batter with a tablespoon measure onto parchment-lined baking sheets. They took exactly 14 minutes to bake to the perfect doneness, still holding their shape with slightest browning on the bottoms. I didn't even need to let them rest on the sheet pans for 5 minutes before removing to cooling racks. I wanted a thicker glaze, so I used confectioner's sugar, lime and lemon juice, and 1/4 tsp. lemon extract. I dipped the tops of the completely-cooled cookies in the glaze, tipping them to let the excess drip off. Garnished with a bit of additional lemon-lime zest. This recipe is a keeper. I can foresee myself making these often, and not just for my family. Thank you so much for this wonderful recipe.

Loved these. Changed the icing by making a very thin lime juice/confectioner's sugar icing and dipping the cookie tops in, letting the excess run off. Before the icing set, I topped with additional grated lime zest. These were a huge hit.

Totally awesome soft cookies. I was making a heavy, spicy meal and just wanted a light bite of something fresh for dessert. I stumbled over these cookies and decided to give them a try. I read earlier reviews and used half milk/half whipping cream. I used two TABLESPOONS of lime juice in the batter. On a whim, to add some texture, I added a half cup finely chopped, toasted pecans. I chilled the dough before dropping teaspoonfuls onto parchment papered cookie sheets. A 10 minute cook time was perfect. I added 1 tablespoon of cream cheese to the lime juice and powdered sugar glaze to give it some body. The taste was great but the consistency was just too thin. Next time I am going to try using a light lime flavored icing. These were still a hit for a fresh, light dessert.

Super yummy cookies. I added 1T. zest and 1/3 cup more of flour to the batter which made it a bit thicker so I could drop them immediately. I heated the glaze 20 seconds in the microwave and let it cool so it was easy to brush on the cooled cookies because the sugar was dissolved. I also added 1 1/2 tsp grated zest to the glaze. Perfection

Mine needed more time in oven - probably 15 mins - and stuck badly to the pan. Hadn't read enough reviews and may try again, refrigerating dough beforehand and trying parchment lined pan. I made glaze with powdered sugar and it definitely helped flavor. Don't know how they'd hold up overnight however. These are definitely more cake than cookie like. A guest added fresh blueberry jam on top and that was a winning combination! Flavor of these is nice but do think they're a bit doughy.

I wish the expected number of cookies were included in this recipe, also, I made more than the mentioned amount of glaze, stepping up to 1 cup of sugar, (I used confectioners sugar with the recipe did not specify) and as much lime juice as needed to make it work. I also added some lime zest to the glaze. Easy recipe, great cookies.

I made a couple adjustments. Added 2 tsp rose water along with the lime juice. I had some organic dried rose petals on hand so I added some to the cookie dough. Put more crumbled rose petals, and lime zest, into the glaze. It made them look quite festive!
Absolutely delicious! I will be making these again. I added sweetened coconut with the lime zest, and for the glaze I used Grapefruit juice. Absolutely superb!

My daughter's church requests that the previous years confirmation canidates families provide cookies for the current years reception. So this year I was asked to bake three dozen cookie since my daughter was confirmed last year. So Even though I am not Catholic I cheerfuly started looking for recipies for cookies. I was determined to make something nice and interesting and that tasted like spring. I had Fresh Strawberries and Limes so with those ingredients in mind I went looking. Low and behold I found this! I read the reviews and I was impressed so I tried it and I was not dissapointed. the reception only got a dozen my daughter and I ate the rest and sent the others to the reception. I made more about a week later only the second time I doubled the lime the second time and it was even better and I also recommend heating the lime juice for the glaze before you add the sugar so it melts completely, making a simple syrup it sets up nicer and isn't gritty. I then sprinkled colored sugar on it which was very pretty!

Everyone loved them. Very soft and not overly sweet. I tweaked the recipe a little and added lemon as well as lime then toped it with a powdered sugar lemon lime glaze. I will definitely be making this again.

The cookie was soft but bland. I wish it had a much more intense lime flavour. I could barely taste it! And I did the glaze with white sugar which didn't turn out the best. It wasn't enough to cover all of the cookies and I personally didn't like how sugar crystals still stayed. So I'd recommend trying to melt the sugar with the lime juice or just using powdered sugar. And using more lime juice.

The texture of these cookies is lovely -- soft, light, & moist. My only complaint is that I wish they had tasted more strongly of lime (I followed the recipe as written, except that I used confectioner's sugar for the glaze rather than white sugar). Still, a nice recipe that was a crowd-pleaser at the office.
Needs a pinch more flour. Wonderful flavor
I think I added too much flour as the cookies did not spread, completely my bad though since I live in a dorm and do not own scales nor measuring cups 😂 They turned out really cute nonetheless!
Delicious recipe! I changed the milk for some heavy cream instead and forgot to buy eggs so it worked great with a tablespoon of Mayo instead.

These cookies had very little flavor and didn't bake correctly - for some reason they were never able to bake fully no matter how long they were in the oven (the dough was really moist). The glaze also was never able to set on the cookies. Will not be making these again.

so delicious! the dough was very soft, so i allowed it to become more firm in the fridge before baking. i also used powdered sugar for the glaze instead of white sugar. my loved ones were obsessed with them! saving this
This recipe was about as expected although the glaze never really set for me - it just kind of seeped into the cookies. However, the cookies were soft and chewy which was excellent!

This cookie comes out soft and delicious! I used confectionary sugar for the icing and used more than it called for in order to make it thicker. I also added two drops of Lime Essential Oil from DoTERRA. (Lime oil comes from the fruit’s rind. If you squeeze a small piece of rind while holding it up to the light, you will see it squirt out the oils captured inside.) This punched up the lime flavor
